reader.requirement: At COBOL-85, FUNCTION FACTORIAL of a positive integer argument-1 must return n! exactly as an integer, without the 18-digit composite-of-operands limit (§1985:IV.4.3.4), within the implementor's documented technique for evaluating integer functions.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 edition window sig.IntroducedIn > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel / RemovedIn (COBOL1502/COBOL1503); the catalog row carries IntroducedIn 85, so --std 85 admits the function

ConstructRegistry numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002: at 85 a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (MOVE, DISPLAY, ADD operand, PERFORM n TIMES) is COBOL0900 per §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4; inside an arithmetic expression it is not consulted

OPTIONS paragraph (2002) and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL (2014) are refused at 85, so the renderer's num.StandardDecimal arm is unreachable and only the native arm runs (the same arm 2023 takes without an OPTIONS paragraph)

DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal: at 85 an unphrased size error (e.g. FACTORIAL(34) past the documented Int128 intermediate) continues with the resultant undefined (§1985:VI.6.4.2); at 2023 it is fatal EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW

reader.edition-search: grep for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior|ConstructRegistry over IntrinsicRenderer.cs, NumericRenderer.cs, IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs, IntrinsicCarrierRules.cs, FunctionValueLane.cs and src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Intrinsics/*: no hit; the only edition reads on the path are in IntrinsicBinder (window, placement) and the OPTIONS gates in VersionConformancePass
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the returned value; yes for the size-error disposition when n! exceeds the native Int128 intermediate (n >= 34) and no ON SIZE ERROR is written: 85 continues with the resultant undefined, 2023 ends the run unit with EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness checks 2! = 2, 5!/4! = 5 and 3!/2! = 3 relations; exact values past 18 digits, a P-scaled integer item, an ODO element, a self-modified argument and the carrier limit are not exercised

probes.printed: FACTORIAL(34) ON SIZE ERROR: SIZE ERROR; unphrased: program continues, R18=000000000000000000 (at --std 2023: fatal EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW)
probes.expected: 34! exceeds the implementor's documented native intermediate (Int128, DOC-A.1-123; §1985:IV.4.3.4 'Each implementor will indicate the techniques'); unphrased size error leaves the resultant undefined and continues (§1985:VI.6.4.2)

probes.printed: COBOL1504: FUNCTION FACTORIAL takes 1 argument(s); 2 given
COBOL1627: argument-1 is the numeric literal 2.5, whose value is not an integer
COBOL1627: a numeric data item with digits to the right of the decimal point
probes.expected: refused: not an expression that always results in an integer

probes.printed: COBOL1627: argument-1 is FUNCTION SIN, a numeric function, ... bars from an integer operand position
probes.expected: refused by §1989:A.2.3 (a numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required)
an integer function is admitted where an integer is required; 2! = 2

probes.printed: COBOL0804 / COBOL0900: OPTIONS and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL refused at 85
probes.expected: only native arithmetic exists at 85, so the FactorialDec standard arm is unreachable

reader.notes: n! is exact up to 33! (20!/1000 and 33!/32! prove values past 18 digits are carried, as IV.4.3.4 requires); 34! and above raise the size error on the documented Int128 native intermediate (DOC-A.1-123), which §1985:IV.4.3.4 leaves to the implementor. The 85 arm of the unphrased size error (continue, resultant undefined) matches §1985:VI.6.4.2.

refuter.evidence: f7zero.cob: FACTORIAL(25)/FACTORIAL(24)=25 (25! is 26 digits, carried exactly). FACTORIAL(34)/FACTORIAL(33) ON SIZE ERROR fires the handler (R unchanged) although the final 34 fits: CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#Factorial throws CobolSizeError for n>33 on the Int128 carrier. The CONFORMS reading holds on §1985:IV.4.3.4 'The implementor specifies the representation of integer and numeric functions' (a representation has a finite range; DOC-A.1-123 documents the Int128 native intermediate). Note (not this rule): §1985:VI.6.4.2 lists only three size-error circumstances, none an intermediate that cannot be formed, so ON SIZE ERROR firing for 34!/33! is an implementor-limit disposition, not text-directed. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.14.4 RV2; OK §1985:IV.4.3.4; OK §1985:VI.6.4.2 (GR2).
